neighbours.label: the comma directly after a conjunction or relative pronoun that suspends the clause for an inserted phrase ('and, to remove all doubt, …', 'who, having been …'), in long periodic sentences; short modern sentences with the same comma do not fire
fire: Now the king, hearing that the city had been delivered, gave thanks in the temple before all the people; and, to show that his vow was not forgotten, he sent gifts of gold to the priests who had kept the gate.

The caravan was overtaken in the desert by a troop of robbers, who killed all the merchants except the guide, who, having been wounded in the first assault, was left for dead among the camels and so escaped.

When the brethren had finished their prayers, the abbot called the stranger into the chapter house; and, to remove every suspicion from their minds, he caused the letter to be read aloud before the whole company.
The ship was driven upon the rocks in the night, and the sailors were cast into the sea, save only the boatswain, who, being a strong swimmer and knowing the coast, reached the shore before dawn.
They for whom the ransom was paid were set free from their chains, and, returning with gladness to their own country, they built an altar unto the Lord in the place where they had wept.
The governor received the envoys with great courtesy in the hall of the palace; but, fearing that the people would rise against him, he kept them under guard until the fleet had sailed.
The old soldier told them of the siege and of the hunger within the walls, and of the captain, who, having refused to yield after forty days, was at last betrayed by his own servant.
The widow gave all that she had to the poor of the village, trusting in the mercy of heaven; and, that no man might praise her for it, she did it secretly and by night.
quiet: Now the king heard that the city had been delivered and gave thanks in the temple before all the people, and he sent gifts of gold to the priests who had kept the gate.
The caravan was overtaken in the desert by a troop of robbers who killed all the merchants except the guide, and he was left for dead among the camels and so escaped.
When the brethren had finished their prayers, the abbot called the stranger into the chapter house and caused the letter to be read aloud before the whole company.
The ship was driven upon the rocks in the night, and the sailors were cast into the sea, but the boatswain was a strong swimmer and reached the shore before dawn.
They for whom the ransom was paid were set free from their chains and returned with gladness to their own country, where they built an altar unto the Lord.
The governor received the envoys with great courtesy in the hall of the palace but kept them under guard until the fleet had sailed.
The old soldier told them of the siege and of the hunger within the walls, and of the captain who was at last betrayed by his own servant.
The widow gave all that she had to the poor of the village and trusted in the mercy of heaven, and she did it secretly and by night.

notes: Probes: long archaic sentences with 'and,' / 'who,' 0.87-1.01, German 'und -' 0.90, French 'sont peut-être' 0.47; the same comma in short modern sentences 0.03-0.06; long archaic sentence without it 0.12.
